title: transaction-cost-sensitivity-simulator-and-onboarding-playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document introduces the Transaction Cost Sensitivity Simulator (TCSS), a lightweight simulation and onboarding playbook for customers and internal sales/product teams to estimate how micro-level configuration choices (batching, kv-cache, quantization profile, fallback routing) and traffic patterns influence transaction-level cost, average latency, and perceived fidelity. The simulator is intended to be used in pre-sales conversations, self-serve onboarding flows, and as an input to fidelity/packaging recommendations in Redwood Optimize.

Scope:
- Valid for hosted and dedicated deployment surface; private deployments are supported for architecture but require a separate local-run instruction set.
- Focuses on conversational and transactional generation workloads (single-turn and short multi-turn).
- Not a replacement for runtime load testing; it provides scenario-level estimations to guide pricing/packaging decisions.

Why this exists:
- Customers repeatedly ask for a quick way to project token-level cost across different fidelity and latency settings before committing to Dedicated or purchasing fidelity credits.
- Sales and Solutions Engineers need reproducible examples and a step-by-step runbook to walk customers through tradeoffs.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Transaction: A single API call as the customer would bill it (includes prompt + response tokens + any embeddings used for retrieval).
- Fidelity profile: A named bundle of model variant, quantization level, and decoding constraints (e.g., "high-fidelity", "balanced", "low-cost-quant").
- Effective token cost: unit token cost after batching and cache savings applied (computed by simulator).
- Per-transaction latency: 95th percentile latency estimate derived from base model latency and multipliers for batching, caching, and regional routing.

Components

1) TCSS engine (service name: consumption-sim)
- Input: workload spec, traffic distribution, fidelity profile set, runtime policy knobs.
- Output: CSV of per-transaction estimates (tokens_out, tokens_saved, effective_unit_cost, estimated_latency_p95, fallback_probability).
- Estimation primitives: prefix-KV hit-rate model, batching distribution sampler, quantization-cost table, kernel-latency lookup.

2) Onboarding playbook (this doc)
- Guided steps for internal SRE/SE or external customer to run scenarios, interpret results, and convert to recommended packaging (credits / reserved capacity).

3) UX/Artifacts
- A one-page PDF summary for customers showing three scenario cards (Conservative, Expected, Aggressive savings) and recommended commercial levers.

Simulator specification (high level)

Inputs (example items):
- traffic_profile: distribution of sequence lengths and request arrival rates (rps, burstiness factor)
- fidelity_profiles: list of {name, model_variant, quantization, beam/temperature constraints}
- cache_policy: {kv_hit_rate_estimate, prefix_cache_enabled_boolean}
- batching_policy: {target_batch_size, max_latency_ms_budget}
- routing_policy: {prefer_low_latency_region, allow_variant_fallbacks}

Example input (JSON-style for copy/paste):
{
  "traffic_profile": {"rps": 30, "burst_factor": 2.5, "sequence_length_p50": 120, "sequence_length_p95": 512},
  "fidelity_profiles": [{"name":"balanced","model":"rw-7b-v2","quant":"int8","max_tokens":256}],
  "cache_policy": {"kv_hit_rate_estimate":0.18, "prefix_cache_enabled":true},
  "batching_policy": {"target_batch_size":16, "max_latency_ms":220},
  "routing_policy": {"prefer_low_latency_region":true, "allow_variant_fallbacks":true}
}

Outputs (CSV columns produced by consumption-sim):
- scenario_id, fidelity_profile, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, tokens_saved, effective_unit_cost_usd_per_token, transaction_cost_usd, est_latency_p50_ms, est_latency_p95_ms, fallback_trigger_rate

Important model and hardware knobs used by the engine:
- model_base_latency_ms: per-variant baseline per-token latency (from runtime-architecture/kernels)
- kernel_multiplier_by_quant: multiplier table that maps quantization profile to relative throughput (e.g., int8 -> 0.6 vs fp16 -> 1.0)
- batching_latency_overhead_ms: modeled startup and scheduling overhead as a function of batch size
- kv_cache_saving_pct: estimated percent reduction in generated tokens when prefix cache hits (depends on sequence length distribution)

Pricing and packaging guidance (how to turn results into commercial recommendations)

1) Map per-transaction cost ranges to three purchase suggestions:
- Developer trial: up to 10k transactions/month — recommend Hosted API with "balanced" profile and 10% credit buffer.
- Production small: 10k–1M transactions/month — suggest Warm Capacity subscription or micro-bundle credits with a recommended quantization experiment.
- Dedicated candidate: >1M transactions/month or high-compliance needs — run a dedicated-sim with fleet sizing and SLA uplift; include dedicated warm pools.

2) How to recommend fidelity credits: use the Conservative/Expected/Aggressive savings cards from the simulator. Convert token savings into credit pairs: tokens_saved_per_month -> fidelity_credit_delta and present a 3-tier quote.

3) Risk indicators that trigger a deeper engineering evaluation:
- Simulator predicts >30% fallback probability due to saturation under realistic burst patterns.
- Effective_unit_cost delta between balanced and low-cost profiles < 5% (indicates poor cost differentiation — investigate kernel selection).

Onboarding playbook (step-by-step)

Prerequisites:
- access to the TCSS web UI and the consumption-sim CLI (internal) or a recorded run exported as CSV.
- a representative prompt set or traffic recording (use developer preflight kit if the customer lacks recordings).

Steps to run a basic customer scenario:
1) Collect customer workload sketch: typical prompt lengths (p50, p95), expected monthly transactions, latency SLOs.
2) Load traffic profile into TCSS via UI or consumption-sim CLI: consumption-sim run --input workload.json --profile balanced --out results.csv
3) Compare three fidelity profiles: balanced, high-fidelity, low-cost-quant. Run each and export results.
4) Create summary cards: show per-transaction cost, monthly extrapolation, and estimated SLA compliance (pct transactions under latency SLO).
5) Recommend packaging option and an experiment plan: A/B quantization or small dedicated warm pool trial for 30 days.

Sample CLI session (internal):
# run simulator with sample workload
consumption-sim run --input sample_workload.json --profiles balanced,low-cost-quant,high-fidelity --batching-config small-latency --out results/sample_run_2027-01-10.csv

Interpreting results (quick heuristics):
- If tokens_saved > 15% and effective_unit_cost decreases by >20% for low-cost profile, recommend a staged quantization rollout and a microbundle.
- If est_latency_p95 for balanced profile exceeds customer SLO by >150ms while low-cost profile meets SLO, highlight that latency-based routing or regional pinning should be considered instead of fidelity reduction.

Rollout and release plan for TCSS (internal timeline)
- Alpha (internal SEs): complete by 2026-12-15 — basic CLI + CSV outputs, three built-in fidelity profiles.
- Beta (closed customers): 2027-01-15 — add web UI scenario cards and PDF export for customer sharing.
- GA (public): 2027-02-28 — integrate into onboarding flow and Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Success metrics (KPIs)
- SE usage: 50 guided runs per month in first quarter post-GA.
- Sales impact: reduce time-to-quote by 30% for large deals involving fidelity questions.
- Accuracy: simulator median estimate within 10% of measured per-transaction cost in 70% of pilot runs.

Monitoring and validation
- Each TCSS run logs inputs and outputs to datalake (tagged with scenario_id). Periodic replay against a small subset of customers with sampled real traces to measure deviation.
- Alerts: >20% divergence between simulated and measured monthly spend for any account should create a ticket in "consumption-sim-validation".

Appendix A — Fidelity profile examples
- balanced: rw-7b-v2, int8, soft-penalty decoding (typical dev defaults)
- high-fidelity: rw-14b, fp16, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95
- low-cost-quant: rw-7b-v2, int4, aggressive-token-filtering
